sections.html:
A quick West Allis sale starts with a decision about the buyer: someone using a mortgage, someone you find yourself, or a buyer paying cash. Each one meets the same three Wisconsin requirements. Namely a condition report for the buyer, an electronic transfer return for the state and a deed on record with Milwaukee County. Taking a mortgage out of the picture drops the loan and appraisal steps, which is where most listings lose weeks.

West Allis sits in Milwaukee County. The 2025 population estimate is 60,119, a touch under the 60,325 counted in 2020, across 11.38 square miles of land.

The city is dense, with modestly priced homes and a lot of renters. Owners live in 55.5 percent of the homes, and half of owner-occupied homes are worth more than $203,800. Your house competes with plenty of rental stock, so condition and presentation carry weight.

The 2020 census counted 29,015 housing units, 5.2 percent of them vacant. Interstates 94 and 41/894 cross the city, so commute questions are common. Planning a December listing? Candy Cane Lane, on Oklahoma and Montana Avenues between 92nd and 96th Streets, draws heavy traffic on holiday nights, which can complicate showings on those blocks.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin law asks of you
sections.html:
Sell a building of up to four units and you owe the buyer a finished condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. Under chapter 709, a buyer who is left empty-handed can cancel during the following two business days and take deposits back. A personal representative, trustee or conservator who never lived in the house can skip the form, as can a seller whose transfer the fee statute exempts.

The state also charges the grantor a transfer fee, set by s. 77.22 at 30 cents on each $100 of value. Payment comes from the seller at recording. Wis. Stat. 77.24 divides the money, 20 percent to the county and the balance to the state. Exemptions appear in s. 77.25. Inheritances, certain parent-to-child transfers made for nominal consideration, and a foreclosure deed to the mortgage holder all appear there.

Your deed will be recorded downtown at 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds. Each document costs $30, and every conveyance needs the electronic transfer return receipt attached. No cards here: cash, a check or a money order only.

Documents are recorded as they arrive, within three to five business days, and the original is mailed back one to two weeks later. Trouble with the electronic return? The Wisconsin Department of Revenue answers at (608) 266-1594. Drafting and legal advice are outside what the register's counter does, so sellers bring in a title company or attorney. Questions about a pending recording go to (414) 278-4005.

sections.h2: Property taxes and back taxes in West Allis
sections.html:
West Allis taxes are billed by the city. Ahead of listing, phone the City Treasurer about due dates and installments, and the City Assessor about your assessed value and property record. Wisconsin assessors value property at what a private sale would bring, and at closing the title company splits the current-year bill.

The Milwaukee County Treasurer handles delinquent taxes for 2024 and earlier. That office serves every municipality in the county but the City of Milwaukee, and West Allis falls inside its coverage. State law attaches a delinquency charge of 18 percent a year, which makes early payment worthwhile. A call to (414) 278-4033 starts a payment plan. Online payment carries the processor's 2.55 percent card fee, or $1.50 if you use an e-check.

Owe back taxes? A payoff figure from the Treasurer, obtained before you agree to anything, keeps your comparison honest. Your closing agent pays that balance out of the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a West Allis owner?
sections.html:
Gather written terms from every buyer and line the options up.

  • Agent listing. A good match when the house looks presentable and no deadline presses.
  • For sale by owner. You pocket more of the price, and you also shoulder the disclosures and the haggling.
  • Cash buyer. Suited to houses needing repairs, inherited or rented properties, and owners racing a foreclosure. Compare the net after title and recording costs.

Gather what a West Allis buyer will ask for before you list. Start one folder: the vesting deed, a current mortgage statement, the newest tax bill and repair records. The assessor's property record is worth printing, since it shows your assessed value and the details the city holds on the house.

A house from an estate needs documents proving who may sign the deed. If foreclosure is a worry, speak to a title company early. A sale can still close when the numbers work, and a cash offer can move on a date you pick.

sections.h2: Weighing offers against what you keep
sections.html:
Price alone can mislead. In a city this built-up, no buyer is short of choices, so the terms you can offer matter. A listing offer that depends on a buyer's loan may fall through at the appraisal, and a lower cash offer may close sooner and cost you less while you wait. For each offer, subtract the transfer fee, any tax balance, repairs the buyer wants and the months of upkeep before closing.

Settle who pays for title work and recording, and see that the offer says so. Behind on the mortgage? Then a reliable closing day may be worth more than a few extra dollars, and each buyer should tell you how quickly they could close.

sections.h2: Questions to put to your title company
sections.html:
A West Allis sale involves a few figures that only your closing agent can pin down. Learn the exact mortgage payoff, and whether a tax balance must be cleared alongside it. Find out how the current-year tax bill gets split with the buyer, and what the county register expects to see attached to the deed.

Confirm who files the electronic transfer return and by when, since a deed without it is turned away. Written answers collected ahead of closing mean fewer surprises on the settlement statement.

When you accept an offer, the report clock starts, so complete the form right away. Behind the scenes, the title company checks the records and gets the deed and return ready. At the table you sign the deed, the transfer fee is paid, and the mortgage or tax balance is settled out of proceeds. The register's office then records the deed. A cash deal takes the same steps without the lender appraisal, so the title search and recording set the pace.

faqs.q: How quickly can a West Allis house sell?
faqs.a: It turns on the buyer. A buyer who needs no loan skips approval and appraisal, which leaves the date to title work and recording. Financing brings showings, inspections and underwriting.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: Each document is $30, and the transfer fee on your return receipt is added. Pay by cash, check or money order, because cards are refused.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property taxes in West Allis?
faqs.a: The Milwaukee County Treasurer does, for 2024 and earlier years, across the county apart from the City of Milwaukee. The delinquency charge set by state law is 18 percent a year. Call (414) 278-4033 about a payment plan.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: No, provided you are a personal representative or trustee who never lived there. Chapter 709 excuses those fiduciaries. Under s. 77.25 a transfer by will, descent or survivorship also avoids the transfer fee.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a West Allis sale?
faqs.a: The grantor pays it at recording, at 30 cents for every $100 of value. The electronic return goes to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue.
